title: Add manifest hash locks and rollback sanity checks for private upgrades
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds deterministic manifest hashing and pre/post upgrade sanity checks for private deployments. Installer will compute and persist a manifest-hash.lock for each release, verify backups against that hash before restore, and abort upgrades if post-upgrade health checks fail. Improves safety for rollback paths and reduces risk of partial upgrades.
description: Motivation: we observed a couple of private upgrade incidents where partial resource drift (helm diff + manual v1->v2 schema migration mismatch) resulted in failed rollbacks and long recovery windows. This PR introduces a lightweight manifest hash lock and a set of pre/post upgrade sanity checks in the private installer to reduce blast radius and ensure safe rollback paths. Implementation summary: - compute a canonical manifest bundle (helm rendered YAML + terraform state note) and store SHA256 in a manifest-hash.lock in the release bundle and backup snapshot metadata; - require backup integrity verification before any restore/rollback path; abort if hash mismatches unless force flag provided and operator confirms; - add preflight checks (cluster resource quotas, minimal available PVC size, required KMS access) and post-upgrade health probes (control-plane liveness, DB migration status, kv-cache warmup signal); - add a guarded downgrade blocker that prevents applying manifests with lower semver unless explicit --allow-downgrade is used and manifest hash matches a recorded snapshot; - integrate manifest hash check into terraform module (plan-time validation) and helm chart CI (render + compare); - add automated rollback choreography: snapshot -> apply previous manifests -> verify manifest-hash match -> run post-rollback health probes. Checklist: - [x] compute and persist manifest-hash.lock during build/release - [x] store hash in backup metadata for restore verification - [x] enforce preflight and post-upgrade sanity checks in installer flow - [x] terraform plan-time manifest validation hook - [x] helm rendering test in CI that verifies lock consistency - [x] docs and playbook updated with force/allow-downgrade semantics - [x] e2e upgrade+rollback tests added to perf-canary harness Backwards compatibility: the installer tolerates older backups that lack manifest-hash.lock by falling back to checksum-less restore but emits a high-severity warning and requires operator confirmation. For environments that opt-in to strict mode (config: strict_manifest_lock: true) the installer will refuse any restore that lacks a matching recorded hash. See linked tickets for rollout/opt-in plan. Rollout plan: enable max-safety (strict) on internal test clusters, opt-in for a subset of early access customers, then flip strict by default in next minor release following telemetry. Related: ENG-4823 is the tracking Linear. Links: design notes and playbook: https://linear.app/ENG-4823/design/manifest-locks-and-sanity-checks Testing: unit tests, integration harness, and canary runs documented in testing_notes.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial manifest hashing library, persist hash with backup metadata, add preflight/post-upgrade checks, terraform and helm validation hooks, update docs and tests
review_comments: Ethan Wong: Nice approach — can we keep the canonicalization stable across Go versions? Suggest adding a minimal comment about YAML key ordering.
Maya Thompson: Good catch, added deterministic YAML marshaller (gopkg.in/yaml.v3 with explicit map key sort) and test. See second commit.
Priya Rao: How does this interact with existing backup TTL rotation? If a rotated backup loses the hash we need a detection path.
Maya Thompson: Added backup_store fallback: when hash missing we emit a high-severity alert and require operator confirmation; documented in playbook.
Daniel Kim: CI flakes: helm-render-validate sometimes fails on timestamps in templates — added a template scrub step to normalize metadata timestamps.
Daniel Kim: Approved after CI stabilized.
testing_notes: Added e2e scenario in tests/e2e/upgrade_rollback_test.go that performs: deploy v1 -> create backup snapshot -> deploy v2 with manifest-hash.lock -> simulate failed migration -> run rollback flow -> verify manifest hash match and post-rollback health checks. Canary run executed against perf-canary cluster for three consecutive upgrades without regression.
